Maya (People Ops): Heads-up: two small policy updates effective 2026-04-15. 1) "Emergency Caregiver Leave" (ECL): up to 5 paid days in any rolling 12 months for urgent caregiving (child, elder, immediate family medical emergencies, foster/adoption placement). Half-day increments allowed. 2) "Volunteer Time Off" (VTO): 16 hours/year (1.33 hrs/month) for company-approved volunteering. Full policy link: https://intranet.redwood.example/hr/policies/ecl-vto
Maya (People Ops): Quick operational notes: ECL is distinct from PTO and short-term disability; taking ECL does not change accruals. Managers approve in HiBob within 48 hours; retrospective approvals allowed for emergencies. VTO requires prior scheduling and manager sign-off. No cash-out. 
Omar (Finance): Do we need a payroll code for ECL to track separately?
Sana (Legal): Yes, treat paid ECL as regular wages for tax purposes but keep an ECL code for reporting (we recommend "ECL_PAY"). No benefit eligibility changes. International tax considerations will be documented per region.
Maya (People Ops): Also increasing the emergency family travel reimbursement cap to $2,000 per incident (from $1,000). Pre-approval required for >$500; receipts required.
Omar (Finance): Noted. We'll add the ECL expense tag and update Concur mappings. Corporate card ok when available; otherwise submit as expense with the incident tag.
Riley (Engineer): Quick Q: If my kid gets sent home from school, can I use ECL same day?
Maya (People Ops): Yes, same-day caregiver needs qualify. If it extends beyond ECL, coordinate PTO/unpaid with your manager.
